matched_finding.subcategory: Replication power should not rely on an effect the interventions aim to reduce
matched_finding.description: Replication power should not rely on an effect the interventions aim to reduce: This conclusion is sound only if the replication test is performed in an unprotected condition. The estimate comes from studies without the proposed interventions, but three of the four planned groups are designed to reduce the discussed-versus-non-discussed difference. If the memory conformity effect is tested as an omnibus main effect across all participants, successful interventions would shrink the average effect; in the limiting case where the three intervention arms eliminate conformity, the group-averaged contrast would be about one quarter of the control contrast. Define the replication test as a control-condition test, or provide a separate power justification for the omnibus test under plausible intervention effects.
matched_finding.quote: Under such conditions, the sample size required for $90 \%$ power was 18 . As a much larger sample was assumed, it can be stated that the power to detect the memory conformity effect will be sufficient.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Counterbalancing removed — must know item confounds are fatal for within-subjects discussed/not-discussed comparison
ground_truth.original_snippet: In order to counterbalance the discussed details, 50% of the pairs will discuss different critical details than the other 50% of the pairs. For example, half the pairs will talk about Eric's cap color but without discussing his company logo (version A of the discussion), while the other pairs will d...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric's cap color and his company logo.
ground_truth.description: Removed item counterbalancing — without it, discussed vs non-discussed comparison confounds item difficulty with experimental manipulation

matched_finding.subcategory: Discussed-item contrast may be confounded in Section 3
matched_finding.description: Discussed-item contrast may be confounded in Section 3: The discussed-versus-non-discussed contrast appears to be confounded unless the item assignment is actually counterbalanced. Section 2.3 says that discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but the Procedure section also says each pair, and apparently all pairs, will discuss the same four critical details. Unless an omitted rotation is intended, discussed status would be confounded with item identity. If the same items are always discussed, the within-subject accuracy difference could reflect item difficulty or salience rather than memory conformity.
matched_finding.quote: Thus, analyzing memory conformity is based on a within-subjects factor. In contrast, the methods of reducing the memory conformity effect constitute a between-subjects factor with four levels (three methods and the control group). The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels (three groups of methods of reducing memory conformity and the control group).

More precisely, if a pair of participants disagreed with each other and gave d...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s ...
ground_truth.description: Removed disputed/non-disputed classification — treats all discussed items as containing misinformation when some may not have; conflates delivered vs non-delivered misinformation

matched_finding.description: Conflicting misinformation scoring in Section 3: The analysis plan appears to use two different rules for coding discussed/misinformation items. It first treats the partner's actual response as determinative, excluding cases where the partner gives the participant's version or says 'don't know,' but then states that all discussed items will be categorized as having contained misinformation. For a registered report, it should be clear whether the main within-subject contrast and the misinformation-consistent response index are based on actual misinformation exposure or on assignment to the discussed-item condition.
matched_finding.quote:
However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, "white mug" (such a situation can happen, e.g., as a result of the partner's guessing), the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer 'don't know' will also not be classified as misleading.

In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.

ground_truth.description: Changed intervention from post- to pre-misinformation — tests encoding prevention instead of retrieval resistance; invalidates IMP theoretical framework which requires post-exposure placement

matched_finding.subcategory: Intervention timing conflicts across rationale and Procedure
matched_finding.description: Intervention timing conflicts across rationale and Procedure: The intervention timing is internally inconsistent: this passage says the methods will be administered before collaborative recall and before misinformation exposure, whereas Section 2.5 (as well as the Extended Warning rationale) administers them after collaborative recall and before the individual memory test, after the co-witness misinformation has been introduced. Because timing changes the theoretical mechanism being tested (post-warning versus pre-exposure inoculation), the rationale and procedure need to align on whether the study tests pre-exposure inoculation or post-exposure warning/remediation.
matched_finding.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect. In reality, it is most effective to prepare a witness before possible misinformation reaches them.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Directional tests but sample sizes match two-tailed — must verify power calculation assumptions
ground_truth.original_snippet: Comparisons among all groups and non-directional significance tests are assumed.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'non-directional' to 'directional' — reported sample sizes (492, 82, 34) are for two-tailed tests; one-tailed would need smaller N, creating inconsistency

matched_finding.subcategory: Directional tests are not aligned with the stated ANOVA power framework
matched_finding.description: Directional tests are not aligned with the stated ANOVA power framework: The surrounding section uses G*Power’s repeated-measures ANOVA framework, where the interaction test is an F test and is not directional in the usual one-tailed/two-tailed sense. If the planned follow-ups will instead use directional contrasts, the manuscript should specify the contrast model, tail, alpha level, and multiplicity rule, and the power analysis should match that plan. If not, remove the reference to directional significance tests and describe the pairwise tests as non-directional ANOVA contrasts.
matched_finding.quote: For the planned comparisons between two groups, which will be necessary if the general interaction is significant, the required sample sizes are 492,82 , and 34 participants, respectively. Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.

ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, the age of the participants in each pair will be matched as far as possible.
ground_truth.description: Removed within-pair age matching — age differences activate authority/deference dynamics that inflate conformity through social influence rather than informational influence

ground_truth.original_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect has little use in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is little cost of disagreeing (although it is still possible that some pressure exists as the p...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'has little use' to 'completely ruled out' and removed experimenter-awareness caveat — overclaims mechanism specificity

matched_finding.subcategory: Opening rationale may overrule normative influence too quickly
matched_finding.description: Opening rationale may overrule normative influence too quickly: The assertion that normative impact is “completely ruled out” seems too strong. A private final test removes direct interpersonal pressure at the reporting stage, but the live collaborative recall phase could still create social pressure or public-commitment effects that carry over to later individual reports.
matched_finding.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing. As for false memories, they are possible on the basis of the reasoning and data presented by Wright et al. (2009).

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Open-ended→forced-choice changes baseline conformity rate and scoring categories — must know format matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will be in the form of open-ended questions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.
ground_truth.description: Changed from open-ended to forced-choice — inflates conformity rates (50% guessing baseline vs much lower); scoring categories (correct, misinformation, other) don't make sense with forced-choice

matched_finding.subcategory: Contradictory format of the individual memory test
matched_finding.description: Contradictory format of the individual memory test: The final individual memory-test format is contradictory. Section 2.5 describes a 20-question open-ended test with scoring categories including other answers and total answers, but this passage says the individual memory test will use a two-alternative forced-choice format. The intended format and scoring basis for the primary dependent variables need to be unambiguous.
matched_finding.quote: In existing research using the MORI technique a two-alternative forced-choice questions test was used as the main index of correctness of answers. One of the alternatives matched the correct answer, that is, the item presented to a given participant. The second one, was the alternative consistent with what the partner was presented with. Accordingly, in the scoring system, items in which, during the discussion, the partner of the participant provided an answer consistent with what the partner was familarised with was treated as misleading the participant (e.g., Ito et al. 2019). In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Co-witness exposure exclusion removed — must know non-exposed participants dilute the effect
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.
ground_truth.description: Removed exclusion of non-exposed participants — including those who received zero misinformation dilutes the conformity effect and biases against finding both the basic effect and intervention benefit
